title: The TW Hya Rosetta Stone Project IV: A Hydrocarbon-rich Disk Atmosphere
question: Spatially constrain the radial and vertical location, abundance, and ortho-to-para ratio of the c-C3H2 hydrocarbon layer in the TW Hya protoplanetary disk to improve the interpretation of the disk's C/O ratio.

data.angular_resolution: typically 0.2'' - 0.4'' native, homogenized to 0.5'' round beam (15-20 au)

what.value: Line catalogue data (frequencies, Einstein A coefficients, upper state energies)

evidence.quote: Table notes: $^{a}$ Line catalogue data from CDMS (cite: Muller05)

what.value: Collisional rate coefficients for ortho and para c-C3H2

evidence.quote: We adopt the collisional rate coefficients hosted on the Leiden LAMDA database (cite: Schoier05) originally computed in (cite: chandra2000) for ortho and para separately.

what.value: Physical conditions (gas temperature, dust temperature, gas density) of TW Hya disk model

evidence.quote: We approximate the emission from TW Hya as a series of radial annular regions, where the physical conditions as a function of height at each radial location are taken from the (cite: Cleeves15) model of TW Hya.

what.value: Disk inclination, position angle, and stellar mass

evidence.loc: Images and Radial Integrated Flux Profiles
evidence.quote: We assume an inclination of $5^\circ$, a position angle of $152^\circ$, and a stellar mass of 0.8 M$_\odot$ to create the Keplerian mask following (cite: Huang18).

evidence.loc: Images and Radial Integrated Flux Profiles
evidence.quote: We assume a distance of 59.5 pc (cite: GAIA16).

recipe.goal: Calibrate visibilities, align flux scales across programs, subtract continuum, and image c-C3H2 transitions with a uniform 0.5'' beam
recipe.method: Calibrate with ALMA pipeline, phase self-calibrate on line-free continuum, scale 2013.1.00198.S flux by ~10% to match 2016.1.00311.S, subtract continuum with uvcontsub, clean with tclean using Keplerian masks and line-specific uv-tapers, and smooth to a 0.5'' round beam with imsmooth.
key_parameters: source velocity = 2.84 km s^-1, inclination = 5 deg, PA = 152 deg, M_* = 0.8 M_sun, distance = 59.5 pc
clean threshold = 3 sigma, final beam = 0.5'' round
assumptions: Keplerian rotation with inclination 5 deg, PA 152 deg, M_* = 0.8 M_sun at 59.5 pc; linear continuum shape

recipe.goal: Extract azimuthally stacked, spectrally integrated radial intensity profiles and total integrated line fluxes
recipe.method: Measure integrated line fluxes within Keplerian masks; use GOFISH on the cleaned 0.5'' image cubes to spectrally align and azimuthally stack spectra by deprojecting Keplerian rotation, then integrate over velocity to get radial profiles.
key_parameters: velocity integration range = 2.5 km s^-1 to 3.18 km s^-1
assumptions: Same disk geometry and stellar mass as Keplerian masking (inclination 5 deg, PA 152 deg, M_* = 0.8 M_sun, d = 59.5 pc)

recipe.goal: Fit observed radial intensity profiles with a grid of 1D non-LTE radiative transfer slab models
recipe.method: Run a 7,150-model grid of 1D non-LTE radiative transfer slab models (nLTErt1d) over radial annuli using the Cleeves et al. (2015) TW Hya physical structure, reconstruct 2D sky images, convolve with a 0.5'' Gaussian beam, extract radial profiles in matching annuli, and evaluate reduced chi^2.
key_parameters: Min H2 column = 10^19 cm^-2; Max H2 column = (1 to 187.5) x 10^21 cm^-2; chi(c-C3H2) = (1 to 1000) x 10^-11 per H; OPR = 1, 3; R_inner = 20, 25, 30, 35, 40 au; R_outer = 80, 90, 100, 110, 120 au; Total models = 7150
assumptions: Physical structure from Cleeves et al. (2015) with disk mass 0.04 M_sun and 6.7x reduced small grains in the surface (1 A_V = 1.27 x 10^22 cm^-2 N_H2); constant c-C3H2 abundance within the slab; LAMDA collisional rates from Chandra & Kegel (2000)

recipe.goal: Confirm ortho-to-para ratio via disk-averaged rotational diagram analysis
recipe.method: Perform a disk-averaged rotational diagram analysis using the unblended, optically thin ortho and para transitions to independently derive rotational temperatures and column densities.
assumptions: Unblended ortho and para transitions are optically thin and in LTE

answer_key.quantity: Integrated flux of blended o/p-c-C3H2 9_{1,8}-8_{2,7} and 9_{2,8}-8_{1,7} (351.96593/4 GHz)
Integrated flux of blended o/p-c-C3H2 10_{1,10}-9_{0,9} and 10_{0,10}-9_{1,9} (351.78157 GHz)
Best-fit total abundance of c-C3H2 (both isomers)

evidence.quote: We find the ortho-to-para ratio of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is consistent with 3 throughout extent of the emission, and the total abundance of both $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ isomers is $(7.5-10)\times10^{-11}$ per H atom, or $1-10$% of the previously published $\rm C_2H$ abundance in the same source.

The best fit models have similar characteristics, and abundance of $(7.5-10) \times 10^{-11}$ per H atom, and extend down to an H$_2$ column density of approximately $2\pm0.5 \times 10^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$.

answer_key.quantity: Maximum H2 column density depth of best-fit c-C3H2 slab (N_max)

evidence.quote: The best fit models have similar characteristics, and abundance of $(7.5-10) \times 10^{-11}$ per H atom, and extend down to an H$_2$ column density of approximately $2\pm0.5 \times 10^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$.

answer_key.quantity: Column density of c-C3H2 in the slab (30 best-fit models)

evidence.quote: To test how much of the spread is due to the degeneracy between the thickness of the layer and the abundance, we also show in Figure 5 a histogram of the product of $\chi_{\rm c-C_3H_2}$ and $N_{\rm max}$ and find that this distribution is much tighter, and corresponds to an approximate column density of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ in the slab of $(1-3) \times 10^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$.
We find $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ comes from a layer near the surface that extends no deeper than $z/r=0.25$.

evidence.loc: $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is located in and above the warm molecular layer in a ring
evidence.quote: While this lower boundary does not directly correspond to a normalized height value of $z/r$ due to the nature of the assumed density profile (a power-law with an exponential taper), we can say that within the radial boundaries of the emission, that the $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ arises above a $z/r$ value of approximately 0.25 based upon Figure 3, and no higher than 0.4.
Based on this sub-selection of models, an inner radius of 25 or 30 au is favored by 2/3 of the 30 models.

evidence.loc: $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is located in and above the warm molecular layer in a ring
evidence.quote: The inner edge of the $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ distribution (25 – 30 au) is consistent with the CO snow line (cite: Qi13c; Zhang17) and/or the dip in CO emission (cite: Huang18) and scattered light (cite: debes2013; vanBoekel16).
Nearly all of the best fit models have an outer radius of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ at $>100$ au, with 110 au favored slightly over 120 au.

evidence.loc: $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is located in and above the warm molecular layer in a ring
evidence.quote: The outer edge of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is located at 110 – 120 au.

answer_key.quantity: Ortho-to-para ratio of c-C3H2 from rotational diagram

evidence.loc: The ortho-to-para ratio of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is consistent with a constant value of 3
evidence.quote: Figure 7 shows the results of the fitting, and we find that the ortho and para lines have consistent rotational temperatures, and the derived ortho-to-para ratio from the column densities is $3.02\pm0.78$.

score_reason: All three ALMA project codes are public, open-source analysis and radiative transfer packages (pykepmask, GOFISH, nLTErt1d) are linked and cited, and the 7,150-model parameter grid is fully tabulated in Table 2. Minor deductions for unstated tclean imaging parameters (robust, cell size, exact uv-tapers), unstated non-thermal linewidth in nLTErt1d, and reliance on the external Cleeves et al. (2015) physical disk profiles.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA data, clearly tabulated integrated line fluxes and slab model parameter grid, and public availability of the exact post-processing and radiative transfer codes (pykepmask, GOFISH, nLTErt1d) make the integrated fluxes, rotational diagram OPR, and radial profile fits strong targets for automated reproduction.
